questions.question: In which of the following states is the Mamallapuram Dance Festival organised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Every year, from early January to early February, the Mamallapuram Dance Festival **takes place for four weeks in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• **Exponents of Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohiniattam, Odissi, and Kathak **gather in this town for this major festival to perform spellbinding performances in **Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathakali, Mohini Attam, Odissi, and Kathak**.
 
• Folk dancers contribute to the atmosphere and provide a touch of the local flavour that keeps everyone enthralled.
 
• The festival draws thousands of visitors from all over the world, turning this tranquil little tourist town into a hive of activity.
 
• This dance can be performed individually or in groups, and there are many powerful solo performances at Mamallapuram each year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tamil Nadu **has a long and illustrious history in the arts and entertainment. **Iyel (Literature), Isai (Music), and Nadagam (Drama)** are three types of entertainment that have their origins in rural folk theatre such as Theru Koothu (Street play).
 
• For popularity and simple entertainment value, several styles of groups and individual dances compete with classical forms.
 
• Tribal people execute a few of the dancing types. 
 
• **Mamallapuram**, also known as **Mahabalipuram**, is a town in Chengalpattu district in the southeastern Indian state of Tamil Nadu, best known for the **UNESCO World Heritage Site** of 7th- and 8th-century Hindu Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram. It is one of the famous tourist sites in India. The ancient name of the place is **Thirukadalmallai**.
 
• **Mamallapuram **was one of two major port cities in the **Pallava kingdom**. The town was named after Pallava king **Narasimhavarman I**, who was also known as **Mahabali**. Along with economic prosperity, it became the site of a group of royal monuments, many carved out of the living rock. These are dated to the 7th and 8th centuries: rathas (temples in the form of chariots), mandapas (cave sanctuaries), the giant open-air rock relief the Descent of the Ganges, and the** Shore Temple **dedicated to **Shiva**.

questions.question: The natural aging of a lake by nutrient enrichment of its water is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eutrophication**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a body of water becomes **highly mineralized and nutrient-rich, **planktonic algae develop rapidly as a result of this.
 
• **Eutrophication** is the process of excessive growth of planktonic algae in nutrient-rich water.
 
• Hypoxia is formed as a result of excessive planktonic algae development, which leads to the death of aquatic animals due to low oxygen levels and the gradual disappearance of the lake.
 
• **Excess phosphorus** is usually always the source of eutrophication in freshwater ecosystems, but nitrogen and phosphorus may play diverse roles in marine habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plankton** is a varied group of organisms that live in water and are unable to swim against the stream. 
 
• **Biomagnification** is the accumulation of a chemical by an organism as a result of water and food exposure, resulting in a concentration that is higher than would have been expected from equilibrium if the chemical had only been exposed to water.

questions.question: Which of the following is the highest mountain of Bhutan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gangkhar Puensum**__.

__
 
• **With an elevation of 7,570 metres (24,836 feet) **and a prominence of 2,995 metres, **Gangkhar Puensum is Bhutan's highest mountain **and the world's highest unclimbed mountain.
 
• Its name means** "White Peak of the Three Spiritual Brothers."**
 
• It shares a border with Tibet. 
 
• A Japanese expedition ascended Liankang Kangri in 1999, a 7,535-meter (24,721-foot) subsidiary peak (not an independent summit) separated from the main peak by a 2-kilometre (1.2-mile) long ridge to the north-northwest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gipmochi** is a mountain in south-central Asia's Lower Himalayas. The peak, which rises to a height of 14,523 feet (4,427 metres), is located on the boundary between the Indian state of Sikkim and Bhutan.
 
• **Kangphu Kang,** also known as Shimokangri, is a Himalayan mountain. It is the world's 107th tallest peak, standing at 7,204 metres above sea level.
 
• **Chomolhari** is a Himalayan mountain that straddles the border between Tibet's Yadong County and Bhutan's Paro region.

• Mosquito-transmitted larvae land on the skin and can then enter the body. The larvae subsequently travel to lymphatic arteries, where they mature into adult worms, thus perpetuating the transmission cycle.
 
• The main symptom of elephantiasis is gross enlargement and swelling of an area of the body because of the accumulation of fluid. The arms and legs are the areas most often affected. An entire arm or leg may swell to several times its normal size resembling the thick, round appearance of an elephant's leg.
 
• **Parasitic worms, commonly known as helminths**, are huge macroparasites with adults visible to the human eye.
 
• Many of them are soil-transmitted intestinal worms that infect the gastrointestinal tract.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. My husband would not be back until late and I decided to settle down in a comfortable chair and read a book.

B. I put the children to bed early and prepared some coffee.

C. It had been a tiring day and I was looking forward to a quiet evening.

D. Soon I was sitting comfortably with a cup of coffee and the book.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'CABD'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**While arranging the parts of the passage, we should find some __grammatical or contextual __connections between them. Also, the first sentence of a passage is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 

__
 
• Sentence C is the independent sentence and introduces what the subject was thinking of doing. It states how the subject had a tiring day and was looking forward to a quiet evening. 
 
• So, sentence C is the first sentence after rearrangement. 
 
• Sentence A describes how the subject knew that her husband would come late and how she decided that she would relax by reading a book. Thus, to maintain continuity, sentence A comes in the second position. Hence, A follows C.__
 
• Sentence B which explains the actions taken by the subject after she decided what to do should come after sentence A, to maintain continuity on the topic. 
 
• Sentence D is the concluding statement of the passage as it provides further information regarding how the subject finally was sitting and reading her book. 

Thus, the correct order after rearrangement is option 3 i.e. CABD.

*So, the correct paragraph is : (**C) It had been a tiring day and I was looking forward to a quiet evening. (A) My husband would not be back until late and I decided to settle down in a comfortable chair and read a book. (B) I put the children to bed early and prepared some coffee. (D) Soon I was sitting comfortably with a cup of coffee and the book.***
